On September 27, 2026, Republican Senator John Kennedy criticized government spending on advertisements promoting President Donald Trump during a Sunday interview on CBS’s Face the Nation, hosted by Margaret Brennan. His comments placed criticism of the spending inside the president’s own party, rather than limiting the dispute to Democratic opponents.

The White House defended the commercials as patriotic public-service announcements. Kennedy’s statement is an objection, not a legal determination.

The Guardian reported Kennedy’s comments, and NBC News reported on a taxpayer-funded advertisement released by the White House. Together, the supplied notes situate the remarks amid scrutiny of the administration’s advertising, but do not provide a complete accounting of spending or establish the legal status of each commercial. Any judgment about legality or the ultimate use of the ads requires evidence beyond the stated criticism and the White House’s characterization.
